title: Tandem Affinity Purification Protocol for Protein Complexes from Schizosaccharomyces pombe
author: Cipak, Selicky, et al.
materials: Rabbit antiperoxidase antibody linked to peroxidase (PAP1)

steps.title: Prepare buffers and keep cold
steps.instruction: Prepare all buffers (IPP150, TCB, CBB1, CBB2, EB) at 4 °C; add protease and phosphatase inhibitors immediately before use; keep all reagents and tubes on ice or in a 4 °C cold room.

steps.title: Resuspend yeast powder in IPP150
steps.instruction: Transfer yeast cell powder to tubes, thaw on ice (~2 min), and resuspend with 3 mL ice‑cold IPP150 per gram of powder.

steps.title: Rotate lysate for extraction
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a rotatory wheel in the cold room (4 °C) and rotate gently for 30 min; optional: sonicate using MSE Soniprep 150 at 6 µm amplitude, 5 cycles of 10 s with 30 s cooling between cycles, minimizing foam.

steps.title: Homogenize lysate and add Benzonase
steps.instruction: If needed, add Benzonase to IPP150 to 20 U mL⁻¹ and MgCl₂ to 1 mM before homogenization; homogenize the suspension in a 300 mL centrifuge tube on ice using the same sonicator settings.

steps.title: Clarify lysate by high‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Transfer lysate to clean tubes and centrifuge at 40,000 g for 10 min at 4 °C; repeat supernatant transfer and centrifugation three additional times (total four spins).

steps.title: Transfer, filter, aliquot, and freeze extract
steps.instruction: Move the cleared extract to 50 mL Falcon tubes; optional: filter through 0.22 µm filter; optionally aliquot 50 µL into a 1.5 mL tube and store at –20 °C for later analysis; snap‑freeze remaining extract in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C (up to 1 month).

steps.title: Wash and resuspend IgG beads
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL Falcon tube, combine 500 µL IgG beads with 10 mL ice‑cold ddH₂O; spin at 400 g for 1 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant; wash beads with 5 mL ice‑cold IPP150 (no inhibitors), spin again 400 g, 1 min, 4 °C, discard supernatant; resuspend beads in 2 mL ice‑cold IPP150.

steps.title: Bind extract to IgG beads
steps.instruction: Add the protein extract to the resuspended IgG beads, mix gently, and incubate on a rotatory wheel at 4 °C for 2 h to allow binding.

steps.title: Wash IgG beads on column
steps.instruction: Load the bead slurry onto an empty Econo‑Pac column, allow gravity flow; wash beads with 10 mL ice‑cold IPP150 (20 volumes) followed by 2.5 mL ice‑cold TCB (5 volumes); ensure beads never dry; pre‑wash the column with ice‑cold ddH₂O and IPP150 before use.

steps.title: TEV protease cleavage of bound proteins
steps.instruction: Adjust bead volume to 1 mL with TCB, add 1 mL TCB containing 400 U TEV protease, mix gently, and incubate on a rotatory wheel at 16 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Collect and combine TEV‑cleaved fractions
steps.instruction: Load the TEV‑cleaved mixture onto an empty Poly‑Prep column and collect the flow‑through by gravity; overlay beads with 200 µL TCB and collect the second flow‑through; combine both flow‑throughs and bring total volume to 2 mL with TCB; pre‑wash the Poly‑Prep column with ice‑cold ddH₂O and TCB before use.

steps.title: Neutralize EDTA with CaCl2
steps.instruction: Add 6 µL of 1 M CaCl₂ to the 2 mL combined sample to neutralize EDTA present in TCB.

steps.title: Wash and prepare calmodulin beads
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL Falcon tube, mix 100–150 µL calmodulin beads with 10 mL ice‑cold ddH₂O; spin at 800 g for 1 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant; wash beads with 5 mL ice‑cold CBB1, spin again 800 g, 1 min, 4 °C, discard supernatant; resuspend beads in 6 mL ice‑cold CBB1.

steps.title: Bind TEV‑cleaved sample to calmodulin beads
steps.instruction: Combine the calmodulin bead suspension with the TEV‑cleaved sample from step 12 in a 15 mL Falcon tube, mix gently, and incubate on a rotatory wheel at 4 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Wash calmodulin beads on column
steps.instruction: Load the calmodulin bead slurry onto an empty Poly‑Prep column and collect by gravity flow; pre‑wash the column with ice‑cold ddH₂O and CBB1 before use.

steps.title: Wash calmodulin beads with CBB buffers
steps.instruction: Wash the bound beads with 1–1.5 mL ice‑cold CBB1 (10 volumes) followed by 0.5–0.75 mL ice‑cold CBB2 (5 volumes); keep beads wet throughout.

steps.title: Elute proteins and collect fractions
steps.instruction: Elute proteins by adding 100–150 µL elution buffer (EB) to the beads, incubate 3–5 min, then collect 8–10 eluate fractions into Protein LoBind tubes; store eluates at –80 °C; optional: analyze 10 % of each fraction by SDS‑PAGE and silver staining.

description: Tandem affinity purification (TAP) protocol has been developed to purify protein complexes from the budding yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Rigaut et al., 1999). We have adapted this protocol for the fission yeast Schizosaccharomyces pombe and used it to isolate various TAP-tagged proteins, including protein kinases (Cipak et al., 2009, 2013), cohesin subunits (Phadnis et al., 2015; Sanyal et al., 2018), monopolin proteins (Rumpf et al., 2010), recombination proteins (Cipak et al., 2009; Sevcovicova et al., 2021) and spliceosomal factors (Aronica et al., 2016; Cipakova et al., 2019; Mikolaskova et al., 2021). The TAP tag used in this protocol consists of a calmodulin-binding peptide and two IgG-binding domains of protein A, separated by a tobacco etch virus (TEV) protease cleavage site (calmodulin-binding peptide−TEV−protein A) (Figure 1). To generate S. pombe cells expressing C-terminally TAP-tagged proteins, refer to our previous work (Cipak et al., 2009).Figure 1Schematic representation and amino acid sequence of the TAP tag Protocols optimized for TAP purification of other S. pombe protein complexes have been previously published (Gerace and Moazed, 2015; Gould et al., 2004). In addition to calmodulin-binding peptide−TEV−protein A tag, various combinations of tags such as 3xFLAG−TEV−protein A (Zilio and Boddy, 2017) or protein G−TEV−streptavidin-binding peptide (Goodfellow and Bailey, 2014) can be used for TAP-tagging and purification. The basic principles of these protocols are similar and our protocol contains only minor modifications. One such modification is using a Freezer/Mill grinder cooled with liquid nitrogen to prepare cryomilled yeast cell powder for producing protein extracts. The Freezer/Mill is very efficient in breaking S. pombe cells and minimizes protein degradation.
